summary: Pelee Passage Light on the Middle Ground in western Lake Erie: first lit 4 July 1902, its tower replaced in 1975, still an active light. Reached only by boat.

structures.note: 66 ft from the deck of the foundation to the vane (Department). Pier brown, tower white, lantern red. Dismantled 1975; re-erected in Windsor in 1980.
One-storey keepers' building with a helipad, cylindrical light tower at one corner, on a steel caisson (Directory). The CCG list gives the structure height as 28.6 m; not resolved.

staffing.note: Last head keeper named by Lighthouse Friends: Coleman Main, at least 1953 to 1959.

access.note: Accessible only by boat. Site and tower closed.

events.note: Point Pelee (Pelee Spit) lighthouse and fog alarm destroyed by fire on 17 April 1900; the principal keeper trapped under fallen timbers
Steel caisson sunk on the north end of the Middle Ground: 1 January 1901 (Department) or 1 June 1901 (Lighthouse Friends). Not settled.
Specular: the Department issued two warnings respecting her wreck in Pelee Passage
Light placed in operation on 4 July 1902
Steam siren at the Middle Ground operated from 1 October 1902

Schooner Armenia sank about three and a half miles from the Pelee Passage light in May 1906; abandoned by her owners; removal contract $5,850 (Midland Towing and Wrecking Co.). The 1909 report records the removal.
Diaphone fog alarm replaced the steam siren
Steel tower replaced by a new structure with a helipad and a cylindrical light tower; the light was not deactivated

Old tower re-erected in Windsor (Lighthouse Friends: Dean Construction, 1980). The Directory says it was relocated to Lakeview Park when the present light went up in 1975. The sources disagree on the year.

corrections.proposed: 1975 replaced: the 1902 steel tower replaced by a new structure; the light was not deactivated
corrections.why: The Coast Guard list shows the light operating year round in 2026, and Lighthouse Friends and the Directory describe the 1975 change as a replacement tower, not a deactivation.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record says sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The Coast Guard list (undated web edition) shows entry 602 as a light operating year round, Flash 1 s; eclipse 3 s. The Directory gives it as Active.
The record's position (41.854107, -82.581865) matches the Coast Guard list entry 602 (41 51 14.9 N, 082 34 54.7 W) on the north end of the Middle Ground Shoal.
Directory: relocated to Lakeview Park when replaced in 1975. Lighthouse Friends: dismantled and re-erected in Windsor in 1980 by Dean Construction. Both stated in the story; year not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28 (page images read on archive.org). 1908 report printed p.136 (scan 143): 'Manson, Wm. A. | Pelee Passage, Lake Erie, Light and Steam Siren | Nov. 11, 1902 | 650' confirmed; the OCR reads 'Pellee' for 'Pelee'. The earlier 'column layout' hedge is replaced by the image-confirmed row; the appointment date is left out of the story because the cached OCR does not place it beside the name. 1903 report printed p.57 (scan 234, Appendix 11 above Montreal): 'Bratt, James | Middle Ground, Pelee Passage | Aug. 15, 1902 | 400' confirmed. The same page shows 'Cree, James J | Middle Ground, Pelee Passage | Sept. 3, 1902 | 300', which is not in the cached OCR and so is not cited; it is in the roster as 'other'. Fortier's line (scan 235) was not checked on the image; the story says only what the list gives, with no role or dates. Seen on the 1908 list thumbnail (printed p.136): 'Gaulin, E. J. | Pelee Passage' (appointed August 1904 in the thumbnail, not verified at full size). Not added; a reviewer should check before adding. 1901 report (printed p.33) and p.32: fire 17 April 1900, anchor lantern four days later, 'selected ... because vessels can shape a course directly for it from both directions', 'ready for sinking on the opening of navigation next year', confirmed in OCR. The 1902 report (p.50): 'successfully sunk in 13 feet of water ... January 1, 1901', read in OCR; the page image was not checked. Lighthouse Friends gives 1 June 1901; both are stated. Specular: the two warnings are in the 1902 report (printed p.44), not 1901 as the earlier draft said. Tasmania (1907 report p.31) and Armenia (p.32, 'in May last') read in OCR; confirmed text. The Armenia removal ($5,850, Midland Towing and Wrecking) is in the report printed 1910 (p.49, page not checked on the image). 1903 report: 66 ft tower (p.72 cited; not checked on image), steam siren 1 Oct 1902 (p.46 cited; not checked). Old tower relocation year disagreement (Directory 1975; LF 1980) stated. Current structure height: CCG column 28.6 m; Directory 12 m for the 1975 tower; not stated in the story. The 1905 report's master William Manson (fog stranding) is a different man from the keeper; not used. Point Pelee's 'southernmost mainland point' is LF's wording and is now footnoted. Roster names from LF (Langlois, Bottom, McCormack, Ouelette, Main) are LF-only and not checked against the Department lists.
